title: UK to strengthen cyber defences as minister calls for AI firms to increase safety efforts
key_facts: Kanishka Narayan, the UK's AI minister, will call on companies building frontier AI to do more on safety, in a speech in west London.
He will say Britain cannot rely entirely on technology companies to police their own models and that the UK needs to build more of its own AI infrastructure.
He announces a strengthening of Britain's cyber defences; the Guardian's report gives no detail of what that involves.
Geoffrey Irving, a former chief scientist at the UK's AI Security Institute, told the Guardian that AI companies lack security that would stop an adversarial country stealing models.
OpenAI says it has multiple protections against model theft, including encryption and continuous monitoring.

The speech will be watched for signs the UK may join an international call for common AI safety standards signed by Finland, France, Germany, Australia, Singapore, the UAE and Ireland, but not by the UK or the US.
Satya Nadella of Microsoft called on Saturday for AI models to be designed with an 'emergency brake'.
quote_evidence: Kanishka Narayan will call on companies developing frontier AI to do more to make sure it is safe.
He will say Britain cannot rely entirely on technology companies to police their own models and will argue the UK needs to build more of its own AI infrastructure.
"The AI companies do not have security that would prevent an adversarial country from stealing the models."
why_it_matters_hint: A UK minister signals tougher expectations on AI firms, but the report previews a speech and gives no detail of the cyber measures.
notes: The Guardian's report is a preview ('will say'); the speech itself was not read. No details of the new cyber measures are given.
